summary: @ornikar/jest-config-react preinstall drops Bun runtime to execute obfuscated in-package payload
details: The package's `preinstall` lifecycle hook runs `node setup.mjs`, which downloads the Bun runtime from a GitHub release URL constructed at runtime, extracts it to a temp directory, marks it executable, and invokes it via `execFileSync` to run the sibling file `math_init.js`. `setup.mjs` itself is obfuscator.io-style mangled (hex-prefixed identifiers, wrapper-object dispatch such as `_0x19328d.YCZJE(execFileSync,...)`, Alpine/musl branch detection) to hide the download-and-exec logic. `math_init.js` is a ~711KB Bun-compiled bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs`) with hex identifiers, a rotating string-array decoder (`WV8StW`), and a large numeric-to-character decode table — content unrelated to a Jest/React configuration preset and unreferenced by any Node-reachable code in the package. Using a second runtime to execute an obfuscated in-package payload bypasses Node-only install-time inspection and results in arbitrary code execution on the installer's host on `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
